name: Voidsphere Beholder

alignment.name: Chaotic Evil
alignment.description:
Chaotic evil creatures have a complete disregard for others. They kill, steal, and betray others to gain power. Their word is meaningless and their actions destructive. Their worldviews can be so warped that they destroy anything and anyone that doesn’t directly contribute to their interests.
	By the standards of good and lawful good people, chaotic evil is as abhorrent as evil, perhaps even more so. Chaotic evil monsters such as demons and orcs are at least as much of a threat to civilization and general well-being as evil monsters are. An evil creature and a chaotic evil creature are both opposed to good, but they don’t have much respect for each other either and rarely cooperate toward common goals.
	For the purpose of game effects, a chaotic evil creature is also considered evil.

description: Creatures larger than Medium take up more than 1 square. For instance, an ogre takes up a space that is 2 squares by 2 squares. Most Large and larger creatures also have a reach greater than 1, which means they can make melee attacks against creatures that aren’t adjacent to them. A creature’s basic body shape usually determines its reach; a Large ogre has a reach of 2, but a Large horse has a reach of 1.

traits.name: All-Around Vision
traits.details: Enemies can’t gain combat advantage by flanking the beholder.

traits.name: Truesight
traits.details: The beholder can see invisible creatures and objects.

traits.name: Void Reality
traits.details: The beholder’s attacks ignore all resistances and immunities.

effect.description: The beholder uses one of the following attacks. This attack does not provoke opportunity attacks.
nestedAttackDescriptions: Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Fortitude; 4d12 + 12 force damage, and the beholder slides the target up to 6 squares.
Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Reflex; 6d6 + 17 cold, lightning, and radiant damage, and the target is blinded (save ends).

Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Will; the target takes a free action to move up to twice its speed and make an at-will attack against one of its allies, gaining a +5 power bonus to damage rolls on the attack.

Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Reflex; 4d8 + 20 damage, and the target is removed from play until the start of its next turn. The target returns to play in its original space or the nearest unoccupied space. When it returns to play, the target is dazed until the end of its turn.
Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Fortitude; 3d8 + 10 damage, and ongoing 15 damage (save ends). If this ray’s damage reduces the target to 0 hit points or fewer, the target is destroyed.
Ranged 10 (one creature); +35 vs. Fortitude; ongoing 35 necrotic damage (save ends). If the target is bloodied while taking this ongoing damage, the ongoing damage increases to 40.

failedSavingThrows.name: AverageDamage
failedSavingThrows.description: The target is also dazed (save ends both).

hit.description: Until the end of its next turn, the target grants combat advantage, and if it uses any encounter attack power or daily attack power, it becomes stunned (save ends).

powers.name: Eyes of the Beholder
powers.trigger: An enemy ends its turn within 10 squares of the beholder.

effect.description: The beholder uses one random eye ray against the triggering enemy.
